title: Admin - View Internal Administrators - Accessibility Test Plan (WCAG 2.1 AA)
overview: Accessibility testing of the Admin User Role Management - View Internal Administrators page on the Y4J platform. This page displays a list of internal administrators with their details (name, email, role, status, assigned date, assigned by, permissions). Covers WCAG 2.1 AA compliance for keyboard navigation, screen reader compatibility, visual requirements, form/interactive element accessibility, and dynamic content handling.

testCases.title: Page has proper heading hierarchy for administrators list
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin and navigated to the Internal Administrators page
steps: Open the Internal Administrators page
Inspect the page heading structure using a screen reader or accessibility tool
Verify the page has an H1 heading identifying the page purpose
Verify subheadings follow a logical hierarchy (H1 > H2 > H3)
expectedResults: Page has exactly one H1 heading (e.g., 'Internal Administrators')
Heading hierarchy is sequential without skipping levels
Screen reader announces headings correctly with their level
testCases.postconditions: Page structure is semantically correct

testCases.title: Admin list uses proper semantic list structure
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, administrators list is loaded with at least one admin
steps: Navigate to the Internal Administrators page
Inspect the admin cards container using developer tools
Verify the list of admin cards uses semantic list markup (ul/ol with li) or appropriate ARIA roles (role='list' with role='listitem')
Verify screen reader announces the number of items in the list
expectedResults: Admin cards are wrapped in a semantic list structure
Screen reader announces 'list with X items' when entering the list
Each admin card is a list item
testCases.postconditions: List structure is properly conveyed to assistive technologies

testCases.title: Admin card information is programmatically associated
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, at least one admin card is displayed
steps: Navigate to an admin card using screen reader
Verify admin name is announced as the card heading or label
Verify email, role label, status, assigned date, assigned by, and permissions are all announced with their labels
Check that label-value pairs are programmatically associated (e.g., 'Role: Super Admin')
expectedResults: Screen reader announces admin name as the primary identifier
All data fields (email, role, status, assigned date, assigned by, permissions) are announced with descriptive labels
Information is not conveyed solely through visual positioning
testCases.postconditions: All admin card information is accessible to screen reader users

testCases.title: Role dropdown has accessible name and keyboard support
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin list is displayed with role dropdown visible
steps: Tab to the admin role dropdown using keyboard
Verify the dropdown has an accessible name (aria-label or associated label)
Press Enter or Space to open the dropdown
Use arrow keys to navigate between options (Super Admin / Limited-Access Admin)
Press Enter to select an option
Press Escape to close without selecting
expectedResults: Dropdown receives visible focus indicator
Screen reader announces the dropdown name, role ('combobox' or 'listbox'), and current value
Dropdown opens with Enter/Space
Arrow keys navigate options, screen reader announces each option
Enter selects the focused option
Escape closes dropdown without changing selection
aria-expanded state changes are announced
testCases.postconditions: Role dropdown is fully operable via keyboard and announced by screen reader

testCases.title: Edit Permissions button has accessible name and keyboard activation
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card with Edit Permissions button is visible
steps: Tab to the 'Edit Permissions' button using keyboard
Verify the button has a visible focus indicator
Verify screen reader announces the button name and role
Press Enter to activate the button
Press Space to activate the button
expectedResults: Button receives visible focus indicator meeting 3:1 contrast ratio
Screen reader announces 'Edit Permissions, button' (or similar with context of which admin)
Button activates with both Enter and Space keys
If button is contextual to a specific admin, the accessible name includes the admin's name (e.g., 'Edit Permissions for John Doe')
testCases.postconditions: Edit Permissions button is fully accessible

testCases.title: Tab order follows logical sequence through admin list
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin list is loaded
steps: Place focus at the top of the page
Press Tab repeatedly to move through all interactive elements
Document the tab order sequence
Verify the order follows a logical reading sequence (top-to-bottom, left-to-right for LTR)
expectedResults: Tab order follows: navigation → page heading area → first admin card interactive elements (dropdown, edit button) → second admin card → etc.
No unexpected focus jumps
All interactive elements are reachable via Tab
Focus does not get trapped in any element
testCases.postconditions: Keyboard user can navigate the entire page in logical order

testCases.title: Focus indicator is visible on all interactive elements
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin list is loaded
steps: Tab through all interactive elements on the page
Observe the focus indicator on the role dropdown
Observe the focus indicator on the Edit Permissions button
Observe focus indicator on any other interactive elements (links, navigation)
expectedResults: Every interactive element shows a clearly visible focus indicator when focused
Focus indicator has at least 3:1 contrast ratio against adjacent colors
Focus indicator is not solely a color change
testCases.postconditions: All focus indicators are clearly visible

testCases.title: Text color contrast meets minimum ratio for admin card content
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin list is loaded
steps: Use a contrast checker tool (e.g., axe DevTools, Colour Contrast Analyser)
Check contrast ratio of admin name text against its background
Check contrast ratio of email text against its background
Check contrast ratio of role label text against its background
Check contrast ratio of status text against its background
Check contrast ratio of assigned date and assigned by text
Check contrast ratio of permissions text
expectedResults: Normal text (below 18pt or 14pt bold) has at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio
Large text (18pt+ or 14pt+ bold) has at least 3:1 contrast ratio
All text on admin cards passes minimum contrast requirements
testCases.postconditions: All text is readable for users with low vision

testCases.title: Status indicator does not rely on color alone
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin cards display status
steps: View the admin card status indicator
Check if status is conveyed through text label in addition to any color coding
View the page in grayscale mode
Verify status is still distinguishable without color
expectedResults: Status 'Active' is displayed as text, not solely through a colored dot or icon
In grayscale mode, status information is still clearly conveyed
Screen reader announces the status text
testCases.postconditions: Status information is accessible regardless of color perception

testCases.title: Page is readable and functional at 200% zoom
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin list is loaded at default zoom
steps: Set browser zoom to 200%
Verify all admin card content is still visible without horizontal scrolling
Verify text does not overlap or get clipped
Verify interactive elements (dropdown, buttons) are still usable
Verify the admin list layout adapts responsively
expectedResults: All text content remains readable at 200% zoom
No content is cut off or hidden
No horizontal scrollbar appears for text content
Buttons and dropdowns remain clickable and usable
Layout reflows appropriately
testCases.postconditions: Page is fully functional at 200% zoom

testCases.title: Page content reflows at 320px viewport width
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin list is loaded
steps: Resize browser viewport to 320px width (or zoom to 400%)
Verify all content is presented in a single column without horizontal scrolling
Verify all admin card information is still accessible
Verify interactive elements are still operable
expectedResults: Content reflows to single column layout
No horizontal scrollbar for content (except data tables, images, etc.)
All information remains accessible
No loss of functionality
testCases.postconditions: Page reflows correctly for mobile/zoomed users

testCases.title: Admin list loading state is announced to screen readers
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, about to navigate to Internal Administrators page
steps: Enable screen reader
Navigate to the Internal Administrators page
Listen for loading state announcement while data loads
Listen for completion announcement when admin list is displayed
expectedResults: Screen reader announces a loading state (e.g., 'Loading administrators...')
When data loads successfully, screen reader announces completion (e.g., 'X administrators loaded')
Loading indicator uses aria-live='polite' or role='status'
User is not required to move focus to discover the loading state
testCases.postconditions: Loading state changes are communicated to assistive technology users

testCases.title: Empty state message is accessible when no admins exist
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, no internal administrators exist in the system
steps: Navigate to the Internal Administrators page with no admins configured
Verify an empty state message is displayed
Check that the message is announced by screen reader
Verify the message uses role='status' or aria-live region
expectedResults: Empty state message is visually displayed (e.g., 'No administrators found')
Screen reader announces the empty state message without requiring focus change
Message is within an aria-live region or has role='status'
Message text has sufficient color contrast (4.5:1)
testCases.postconditions: Empty state is communicated to all users

testCases.title: Error notification is accessible when API fails
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, API is configured to fail (or network is disconnected)
steps: Navigate to the Internal Administrators page when API is unavailable
Verify an error notification is displayed
Check that the error is announced by screen reader immediately
Verify the error notification uses role='alert' or aria-live='assertive'
expectedResults: Error notification is visually displayed with clear error message
Screen reader immediately announces the error (role='alert' or aria-live='assertive')
Error message does not rely solely on color (includes icon or text prefix like 'Error:')
Error text has sufficient color contrast (4.5:1)
testCases.postconditions: Error state is immediately communicated to all users

testCases.title: Page has a main landmark region
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, Internal Administrators page is loaded
steps: Use screen reader landmark navigation (e.g., 'D' key in NVDA)
Verify the page has a main landmark containing the admin list content
Verify navigation areas use nav landmark
Check that landmarks have accessible labels if multiple of same type exist
expectedResults: Page has a <main> or role='main' landmark
Admin list content is within the main landmark
Navigation uses <nav> or role='navigation'
Screen reader users can jump directly to main content
testCases.postconditions: Page landmarks enable efficient screen reader navigation

testCases.title: Role label badge has sufficient contrast
testCases.componentElement: Role label badge (Super Admin / Limited-Access Admin)
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin cards with role badges are displayed
steps: Identify the role label badges on admin cards
Use a contrast checker to measure text-to-background contrast of the badge
Check contrast of badge text against the badge background
Check contrast of badge background against the card background
expectedResults: Badge text has at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio against badge background
Badge as a UI component has at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors
Both 'Super Admin' and 'Limited-Access Admin' badges meet contrast requirements
testCases.postconditions: Role badges are readable for users with low vision

testCases.title: No keyboard trap exists on the page
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin list is loaded
steps: Start at the beginning of the page
Tab through every interactive element on the page
Verify focus eventually leaves the page content area (reaches browser chrome)
Open the role dropdown and verify you can close it and continue tabbing
Shift+Tab back through all elements to verify reverse navigation works
expectedResults: Focus moves through all elements without getting stuck
Dropdown can be exited with Escape or Tab
Shift+Tab moves focus backwards through all elements
No component traps keyboard focus
testCases.postconditions: Keyboard users can freely navigate the entire page

testCases.title: Admin card content is accessible without CSS
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin list is loaded
steps: Disable CSS in the browser
Verify the admin card content is still presented in a meaningful order
Verify all information (name, email, role, status, dates, permissions) is still readable
Verify the reading order matches the visual presentation order
expectedResults: Content reads in a logical order: name → email → role → status → assigned date → assigned by → permissions
No information is lost when CSS is disabled
Labels and values remain associated
testCases.postconditions: Content sequence is meaningful regardless of styling

testCases.title: Interactive elements have sufficient touch target size
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin list is loaded on a touch device or responsive view
steps: Measure the clickable area of the 'Edit Permissions' button
Measure the clickable area of the role dropdown
Verify both meet minimum target size requirements
expectedResults: Edit Permissions button has at least 44x44 CSS pixels touch target
Role dropdown has at least 44x44 CSS pixels touch target
Adequate spacing exists between adjacent interactive elements
testCases.postconditions: Touch targets are large enough for users with motor impairments

testCases.title: Page title is descriptive and unique
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin
steps: Navigate to the Internal Administrators page
Check the browser tab title
Verify the title describes the page purpose
expectedResults: Page title includes 'Internal Administrators' or similar descriptive text
Title is unique and distinguishable from other pages
Screen reader announces the page title on navigation
testCases.postconditions: Page is identifiable by its title
